label: mid original phase: non-A token after >=2 earlier A tokens (0,f,d,c,1,o,2,z,p,h,m)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase (95% of mass) at t=3..8, peaking at t=4-6, plus weakly at the <DEL> step (5% of mass). It never fires at t=0-1, and essentially never in the copy phase. It looks like an accumulator over the prefix: the rate rises when earlier tokens come from set A (0,f,d,c,1,o,2,z, then p,h,m). The first token being 0, f, d or c gives about 3x lift, prev2_tok=0 gives 3.5x, and the rate grows with the number of digits. It then fires on a current input outside A, most strongly g, e, v, l, j, b, and mostly on the first occurrence of that token (in_first lift 1.7x vs 0.3x). Top activations look like 0/f/d/c-heavy openings followed by g/v/e/r. Phase+position alone gives recall 0.91 but precision 0.17; adding the A-history condition and a non-A current token raises dev F1 to 0.47 (mass recall 0.75). The remaining signal looks like a graded, token-weighted linear sum that a boolean predicate cannot capture well. The predicate covers 0.84 of top-quartile activations vs 0.52 of the lowest quartile, so strong activations follow the description more closely. I did not isolate which factor drives magnitude.
